first_hunter_context.bar: Q3 2026 diluted EPS consensus $1.52 and revenue $202.3M (Benzinga snapshot 2026-10-02, https://www.benzinga.com/quote/BOH/earnings-forecasts, as reported in search results; the page itself returned 403). Earnings Whispers lists $1.54 (https://earningswhispers.com/transcript/BOH/Q22026 / https://beta.earningswhispers.com/go/w/BOH) and AAII lists $1.53 (https://www.aaii.com/investingideas/article/520346-what-you-need-to-know-about-bank-of-hawaii-corporations-q3-earnings), so three sources agree on $1.52-1.54. The company's own Q2 call guide (https://earningswhispers.com/transcript/BOH/Q22026): margin up about 5bp a quarter to about 2.90% by year-end, assuming one hike in mid-September; Q3 fees about $43M normalized; Q3 expenses about $112.5M; deposit costs 1.25-1.30%; 10-15% of about $2B of public deposits running off in Q3; buybacks of $20M in Q3. My build from that guide: margin about 2.84%, net interest income about $157.5M, revenue about $200.5M (-0.9% against the revenue bar), EPS about $1.51-1.52 (in line). The revenue bar is less certain: Q2 revenue is quoted as $196.9M and as $198.3M by different aggregators.
first_hunter_context.positioning_check: Short interest is 3.5M shares, 8.78% of float, 6.2 days to cover, as of 2026-08-19 (Equibles, https://equibles.com/stocks/boh/shortinterest). Curvedtrading's FINRA series has 12.0 days to cover at the 2026-08-14 settlement against 6.2 on 2026-07-31 (https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/boh/short-interest/, snippet only, page 403). No October settlement was found. That is elevated for a bank but not crowded in the 18-23% sense. Skew: skew_25d_vol_points is null in the baseline. Put/call open interest is 1.83, but total open interest is only 252 contracts and the ATM spread is 63% of mid, so the option market makes no usable directional statement. The event-implied move is 5.65% and only indicative. Tape: BOH closed $80.02 on 2026-07-27 and trades at $70.55 intraday on 2026-10-23, -11.8%; KRE fell from $75.52 to $72.53 over the same period, -4.0% (Yahoo chart v8, https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/BOH?range=6mo&interval=1d and https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/KRE?range=3mo&interval=1d). Over the last 5 days BOH is up +5.1% against KRE +3.9%. Argus cut its target to $66 on 2026-09-30 and Piper Sandler cut from $85 to $78 (Neutral) around 2026-10-01.

evidence.text: First Hawaiian (FHB), BOH's only same-market peer, reported Q3 2026 on 2026-10-23. Its margin rose 5bp to 3.30%, above its own Q2-call outlook of about 3.27%. Its interest-bearing deposit cost FELL 3bp to 1.72% even though the Fed hiked mid-quarter, and total deposits grew $50M to $20.2B, so Hawaii deposit pricing did not reprice up after the hike. BOH guided about +5bp a quarter (2.78% to about 2.83-2.84%) with deposit costs of 1.25-1.30%; if FHB's pattern carries over, BOH's Q3 margin and net interest income land at the top of that path or above it.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: On 2026-07-27 net interest income came in at $153.6M against about $156.7M expected, EPS was in line ($1.47 vs $1.46), and the stock fell -4.7% (baseline). BOH trades on the net interest income line.
evidence.why_not_priced: FHB printed this morning, after BOH's estimates were set (consensus snapshot 2026-10-02). FHB's stock fell about -3.5% today on its credit line (25.225 vs 26.13), so the tape is not rewarding the margin read-across. If it were priced, BOH estimates would have moved up and BOH would have outperformed KRE by more than its +0.3% intraday today.
evidence.independence: This is a peer proxy, not BOH's own number. BOH's balance sheet is different: a lower margin, a 58% fixed-to-float mix and $1.4B of pay-fixed swaps. Management's own statement that a hike helps net interest income at first points the same way (https://earningswhispers.com/transcript/BOH/Q22026). The FHB credit finding below shares the same document.

evidence.text: FHB took a $20.3M provision in Q3 (Q2: $5.6M), driven by a $12.5M partial charge-off on a single CRE loan plus other CRE downgrades. Net charge-offs were 0.60% annualized (Q2: 0.11%) and nonperforming assets rose to $46.0M from $39.5M. BOH's own criticized assets rose to 2.81% from 2.12% in Q2 because of one borrower (93% real-estate secured, about 58% weighted LTV). A charge-off or migration on that BOH credit in Q3 would cost provision against a consensus that assumes about $3-4M.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: BOH's credit line has been quiet: NCOs of 0.03-0.10% and NPAs of 8bp in 2026, and no recent print turned on credit. FHB fell about -3.5% on 2026-10-23 on this line.
evidence.why_not_priced: BOH rose slightly on FHB's print day, so the market did not carry FHB's credit hit over to BOH. If it had, BOH would be down with FHB today. BOH's single-borrower criticized increase from Q2 is disclosed but its Q3 resolution is not.
evidence.independence: BOH's Q2 call disclosed the criticized-asset rise from one borrower (https://earningswhispers.com/transcript/BOH/Q22026). Shares the FHB 8-K with the margin finding above. It is one CRE loan at a different bank, so this is a proxy.

evidence.text: Two hurricanes hit Hawaii in Q3. Lala (2026-08-14) closed BOH branches on Hawai'i Island and Maui; Lowell (2026-09-07/08) closed all BOH branches on Kaua'i. August 2026 visitor arrivals fell -5.6% y/y and visitor spending -9.7% (DBEDT preliminary). The quarter could carry a qualitative reserve build, deferrals or softer card and fee activity, and the call will be asked about Hawaii's outlook.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no prior BOH print that turned on a weather event in the baseline window. The April 2026 Kona-low storms preceded a -0.04% reaction (2026-04-20).
evidence.why_not_priced: The storms are public. No BOH relief or deferral program for Lala or Lowell was found, and FHB's release did not mention the storms; its allowance ratio fell to 1.14% from 1.15%. That argues the transmission is small, which is why this is sized small.
evidence.independence: Visitor data: https://mauinow.com/?p=539526 and https://centreforaviation.com/news/hawaii-records-772000-visitor-arrivals-in-aug-2026-1374086. Lala branch closure: https://www.boh.com/newsroom/bank-of-hawaii-to-temporarily-close-branches-on-hawaii-island-and-maui-county-due-to-hurricane-lala. This is macro-to-company transmission that neither BOH nor FHB has confirmed.

evidence.text: The Fed raised rates 25bp to 3.75-4.00% on 2026-09-16, and the September dot plot implies one more hike in 2026. BOH's year-end margin target of about 2.90% was explicitly conditional on that September hike, and management said hikes help net interest income at first, with a 34% deposit beta. The call can reaffirm the 2.90% exit and extend the path into 2027 on a higher-for-longer curve, which would be the guidance read.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The margin-path guide is what this stock trades on. The 2026-01-26 print, with margin expansion, bought +6.09%; the 2026-07-27 net interest income shortfall sold -4.7% (baseline).
evidence.why_not_priced: The hike was inside BOH's guide, so the direction is known. But BOH fell from $75.43 (2026-09-15) to $66.26 (2026-10-13) after the hike, against KRE -6.7% over the same span, so the market has been pricing the hike as a deposit-cost or AOCI risk rather than as the tailwind management described. A reaffirmed guide cuts against that.
evidence.independence: Guide conditional on the hike: https://earningswhispers.com/transcript/BOH/Q22026 and https://www.webull.com/news/15303749301904384. FHB's CEO says its balance sheet is 'well positioned to benefit from rising interest rates' (FHB 8-K, same document as findings 1-2).

evidence.text: Positioning into the print: BOH is -11.8% since its Q2 print against KRE -4.0%, is 17.7% below its 52-week high, has 8.8% of float short with 6.2 days to cover (August), and has had two target cuts in the last month (Argus to $66 on 2026-09-30; Piper Sandler $85 to $78 around 2026-10-01). An in-line print with a reaffirmed margin path meets low expectations and a moderately heavy short book. The last 5 days, +5.1% against KRE +3.9%, show some of that has already started.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: This is not directly observable in the baseline. The last two prints after drawdowns were 2026-04-20 (-0.04%) and 2026-01-26 (+6.09%).
evidence.why_not_priced: The relative drawdown itself is the market's statement. If the short book had covered, short interest would have fallen and BOH would have closed the gap to KRE; it has closed only about 1 point of an 8-point gap. Short-interest data is from August and may be stale.
evidence.independence: Argus: https://finance.yahoo.com/research/reports/ARGUS_3913_QuantitativeReport_1790726400000. Piper: https://www.thestockobserver.com/?p=8937401. Prices: https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/BOH?range=6mo&interval=1d

evidence.text: The Q2-call guide builds to revenue of about $200.5M and EPS of about $1.51-1.52: margin about 2.84% on about $22.0B of average earning assets after the $200-300M public-deposit runoff, plus $43M of normalized fees, $112.5M of expenses and about $4M of provision. That is about -0.9% against the $202.3M revenue consensus and in line to -2c against the $1.52-1.54 EPS consensus. This name sold off -4.7% last quarter on exactly that pattern, a small revenue miss with in-line EPS.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2026-07-27: revenue $198.3M against $199.7M (-0.7%), EPS in line, stock -4.7%. 2025-07-28: revenue shortfall, stock -4.29% (baseline).
evidence.why_not_priced: The consensus revenue figure appears to sit above the company's own guided components. It may include a different revenue definition (Q2 is quoted at both $196.9M and $198.3M), which is why this is sized small and the bar is flagged as uncertain. If the market already expected a revenue shortfall, the estimate would have been cut toward about $200M by now.
evidence.independence: This is my inference from guidance, not a primary number. Finding 1 (FHB margin beat) points the other way on net interest income; the two net to a roughly in-line quarter, which is why print_vs_bar_pct is -0.5.

evidence.text: BOH planned $20M of buybacks in Q3 and $20M in Q4 (from $89M of remaining authorization). At about $68 average that is about 290k shares a quarter, about 0.7% of shares, against $78 per share paid in Q2. The call may lift the pace with the stock lower.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No print in the baseline turned on capital return.
evidence.why_not_priced: The plan is inside guidance, so only an increase would matter. CET1 of 12.12% (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000046195/000004619526000054/ex991earningsrelease063026.htm) gives room for one.
evidence.independence: The Q2 8-K confirms $17.0M repurchased and $88.9M remaining (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000046195/000004619526000054/ex991earningsrelease063026.htm).

evidence.text: Vice Chair Marco Abbruzzese sold 2,000 shares at $79.84 on 2026-08-03 and his remaining 2,441 directly held shares at $81.59 on 2026-08-04 (Form 4s), about $359k in total, leaving 0 shares held directly. No insider open-market buys were found after the drop; the only later Form 4 is a director's deferred-compensation accrual on 2026-09-30 at $70.54.

evidence.why_not_priced: The sale is small, public and old. It is filed only because the absence of insider buying at $66-70 is the one insider signal available.

first_hunter_context.bar: Q3 2026 operating EBITDA US$953.9m and net sales US$4,506m: Cemex's own compiled consensus of 14 estimates, updated 2026-10-12 (https://www.cemex.com/en/investors/analyst-estimates). Segment EBITDA bars: Mexico 454.6 (+23% yoy), USA 252.0 (-6.4%), EMEA 254.3 (+2.9%), SCAC 67.5. FY2026 EBITDA 3,578 = +16.2% on 2025's 3,080, the low end of the company's 16-17% guide. A second source agrees: MarketScreener Q3 EBITDA 940.1, sales 4,403, FY 3,577 (https://www.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/CEMEX-S-A-B-DE-C-V-6492888/finances/, 2026-10-22). MarketBeat EPS $0.25, revenue $4.45bn (https://www.marketbeat.com/earnings/reports/2026-10-26-cemex-sab-de-cv-stock/). Actinver expects EBITDA about +10% yoy (https://www.bloomberglinea.com/mercados/de-cemex-a-walmex-que-esperar-de-los-reportes-trimestrales-en-la-bolsa-mexicana/, 2026-10-18). The bar is sourced and the sources agree within 1.5%.
first_hunter_context.positioning_check: Short interest 15,650,424 shares at the 2026-09-30 settlement, up 52% from 10,287,321 on 09-15. That is about 1.1% of shares, 2.02 days to cover (https://equibles.com/stocks/cx/short-interest). Not crowded, but building into the print. The option chain is unusable (ATM spread 167% of mid), so there is no skew and no implied move. Put/call OI 0.43. Tape: spot 10.06, -21% from the 12.72 close before the Q2 print, 25.8% below the 52-week high, 20-day run-up +3.6%, 5-day -1.85%. Sell-side: Citi upgraded to Buy on 10-15 (target cut 13.70 to 12.00); RBC trimmed to 13.25 on 10-09; mean target about 38% above spot.

evidence.text: Cemex's FY2026 guide (EBITDA +16-17%, raised 2026-07-23) assumes MXN 18.25-18.50 per USD for 2H26. Banxico's FIX was 17.1277 on 2026-09-14, per Cemex's own dividend 6-K, about 6.5% stronger. Consensus FY EBITDA of 3,578 (+16.2%) still sits at the very bottom of the guide range (3,573-3,604 on 3,080). Mexico is about 50% of consensus FY EBITDA (1,785 of 3,578). So delivering the plan at prevailing FX points to a reiterated-top or raised range, against a bar priced for the low end.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guidance has moved this stock the most. The Q3 2024 guide cut fell -8.7% (close 2024-10-25 5.98 to 10-28 5.46). The Q3 2025 beat with record margins rose +9.9% (9.36 to 10.29, 2025-10-28). But the Q2 2026 raise to 16-17%, together with an EBITDA beat (1,018 vs about 937 consensus), fell -3.6% (12.72 to 12.26, 2026-07-23). Prices are from Yahoo daily bars (https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/CX?range=2y&interval=1d).
evidence.why_not_priced: Fourteen analysts updated by 10-12 still model FY at +16.2%, the guide floor, so the consensus has not credited the FX gap. If the market had priced a guide-top outcome, FY consensus would sit at 3,600+ and the stock would not be 21% below its post-Q2 level with targets cut. Caveat built into the size: analysts likely already model spot FX, so the low-end consensus may reflect expected underlying slippage (energy, US), not overlooked FX.
evidence.independence: The guide and its FX assumption are from the Q2 6-K exhibit (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001076378/000119312526313194/d46310dex1.htm, 2026-07-23). The consensus table is from https://www.cemex.com/en/investors/analyst-estimates (2026-10-12). Peso level confirmed independently: eldolar.info shows 17.78 on 2026-09-28 (https://www.eldolar.info/es-MX/mexico/dia/20260928).

evidence.text: Mexico's construction output rose 7.3% yoy in July and 7.5% in August 2026, with civil engineering +17.6% in August (INEGI industrial activity release of 2026-10-12, via Trading Economics). The Q2 call guided that Mexico's temporary share gains would normalise in 2H and that the margin would dip slightly. Consensus Mexico Q3 EBITDA is 454.6 (+23% yoy, mostly FX) on sales of 1,283 (+14.8%), below Q2's actual 491.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Mexico drove the Q1 2026 print (+6.3%, 11.77 to 12.51 on 2026-04-23) and was the strongest segment in Q2 (+27% LTL EBITDA), yet Q2 still traded -3.6% on the US miss. Net of the rest: the US (-6% consensus) and EMEA (+3%) would have to disappoint by more than any Mexico upside for the total to miss.
evidence.why_not_priced: Industry series, not a company number. If it were priced, the Mexico consensus would sit at or above Q2's 491 rather than 7% below it. Sized small because it is a proxy, and management itself pre-warned of share normalisation.
evidence.independence: CANACEM said Mexican cement sales grew 2% in 1H26 (https://globalcement.com/news/21201-mexican-cement-industry-grows-by-2-in-the-first-half-of-2026), a slower industry rate than the construction series. Actinver and B×+ expect Mexico efficiency gains (https://www.bloomberglinea.com/mercados/de-cemex-a-walmex-que-esperar-de-los-reportes-trimestrales-en-la-bolsa-mexicana/).

evidence.text: The first Atlantic hurricane of 2026 (Isaias) formed only on 2026-10-07, the latest first hurricane on record, so Q3 had no hurricane disruption. On the Q2 call Cemex said 2H US margins should improve if the hurricane season does not disrupt. It also said the Q2 one-offs (temporary aggregate purchases for an Arizona project, a 7% rise in cement imports) would not repeat, and that a mid-single-digit SoCal/Arizona price increase starts in July. Consensus US Q3 EBITDA is 252.0, -6.4% yoy, against a record-margin Q3 2025 comp of 269.3.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: US EBITDA -11% in Q2 2026 coincided with the -3.6% reaction despite a consolidated beat, so the market trades the US line. Net of the rest: a US beat of $10-15m is about 1-1.5% of consolidated EBITDA.
evidence.why_not_priced: A US consensus still below prior year after the Omega acquisition was consolidated suggests analysts carried Q2's weakness forward without crediting the stated non-recurring items or the quiet weather. Weather is an inference, so the finding is sized small.
evidence.independence: The Q2 call transcript summary on US one-offs and price increases (https://www.webull.com/news/15279684413957120, 2026-07-23). USGS: US cement shipments +9.8% yoy in June, +5.1% in 1H26 (https://www.cemnet.com/News/story/182292/us-and-puerto-rican-cement-market-expands-10-in-june.html).

evidence.text: Brent settled at $104.61 on 2026-09-12 after touching $107-109 that week, with US diesel at historic highs. It had been about $83-88 in late July, when Cemex guided cement energy cost only low-single-digit up and 2H energy costs about +4% (about -$20m). About 60% of 2026 energy spend was hedged (Q1 call) and about 80% of 2027 diesel. The risk lands on the 2H/2027 cost commentary and on the Q4 guide.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print turned explicitly on energy. Cemex fell -8.7% on the Q3 2024 guide cut, which is the downside template if the guide is trimmed.
evidence.why_not_priced: Partly priced: Seeking Alpha attributes the 30% drawdown from the May high partly to energy costs (https://seekingalpha.com/mp/1061-the-insiders-forum/articles/6346585-cemex-s-a-b-de-c-v-a-deep-dive, 2026-10-04). Kiln fuels (petcoke, coal) track oil only loosely, and hedges defer the hit. Sized small: it is macro-to-company transmission the company has not quantified since July.
evidence.independence: TASS: Brent fell below $83 on 2026-07-28 for the first time since 07-17 (https://tass.com/economy/2166539/amp). Hedge levels are from the Q1 call summary (https://www.marketbeat.com/earnings/reports/2026-3-31-cemex-sab-de-cv-stock/) and the Q2 call (https://www.webull.com/news/15279684413957120).

evidence.text: JPMorgan's Elodie Rall expects Q3 2026 volumes at European building-materials companies to fall on average versus Q2, on heat-related summer site closures, partly offset by price increases. Cemex EMEA consensus is 254.3 (+2.9% yoy) against a record-margin Q3 2025, and Q2 EMEA was already flat-margined on heat-hit volumes once the $42m one-off is excluded.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: EMEA was not the swing line on recent prints. It carried the Q3 2025 beat (+9.9%). Net of the rest: EMEA is about 27% of Q3 consensus EBITDA.
evidence.why_not_priced: It is a sell-side view on peers, so it is likely reflected in Cemex's modest EMEA consensus. It is a proxy and sized small. Heidelberg's own Q3 update (2026-11-04) falls after the window.
evidence.independence: The Q2 call says the European heat wave restricted work hours and softer demand hit several markets (https://www.webull.com/news/15279684413957120).

evidence.text: Into the print the stock is -21% from the pre-Q2 close (12.72 to 10.05) and 26% off its 52-week high, while FY EBITDA consensus stayed at the guide (3,578). Short interest jumped 52% to 15.65m shares at the 09-30 settlement (still only about 1.1% of shares, 2.0 days to cover), and Citi moved to Buy on 2026-10-15. The price discounts a worse outcome than the published estimates do.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q4 2024 print came off a depressed base (about $6) and moved +13.4% (5.98 to 6.78, 2025-02-06). The Q2 2026 print came off a high base (12.72) and fell -3.6% on a beat.
evidence.why_not_priced: The gap between a price that fell 21% and estimates that did not move is the market's own statement, so this is partly the price itself, and it is sized small. A short rebuild of 5m shares on about 7.7m ADV is a small squeeze fuel at best.
evidence.independence: Citi upgrade and target cut on 10-15 (https://www.ad-hoc-news.de/boerse/news/corporate-news/robeco-boosts-cemex-stake-citi-cuts-target-for-cemex-stock-to-usd-12-00/70382737, 2026-10-21). MarketBeat 200-day moving average 11.65 against spot about 10.06 (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/upcoming-cemex-cx-set-to-post-earnings-on-monday-2026-10-19/).

evidence.text: An aggregator reports that director Zambrano Lozano bought 400,800 Cemex shares for '6.93 million USD', reported on 2026-09-25. The implied $17.29 per unit matches the CPO price in pesos, not USD, so this is most likely a purchase of about MXN 6.9m (about USD 0.4m) of CPOs.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No insider-buy history found for this name.

history.basis: 6-K exhibit text matched results language (8 filings opened). Heuristic, not an item code: a 6-K carrying results language is very likely an earnings release but this is weaker than the 8-K item 2.02 path

options.event_implied_move_basis: 16.28% straddle over 28 calendar days less 14.09% of ordinary 20d-realised movement, subtracted in variance
options.skew_note: IV(25d put) - IV(25d call). Positive = the market is paying more for downside protection than for upside.
warnings: ATM bid-ask spread 60% of mid; implied move is indicative only

baseline.deadband_basis: half the median of 8 prior reactions, floored at 1.5%
baseline.deadband_note: A realised move inside this band is scored as no-direction rather than as a miss.
baseline.expected_move_basis: option straddle net of ordinary vol, front expiry

baseline_quality.note: thin means there is no reliable statement of what the market priced, so a confident call on this name cannot be justified by the baseline.

first_hunter_context.bar: Revenue consensus is $267.4M (Investing.com, 2026-10-23, https://uk.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/makemytrip-earnings-on-deck-as-india-travel-faces-fuel-headwinds-93CH-4928927) and $269.09M (MarketBeat, 2026-10-19, https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/upcoming-makemytrip-mmyt-expected-to-post-quarterly-earnings-on-monday-2026-10-19/). The two sources agree. That bar implies about +17% reported growth against Q2 FY26's $229.3M, which needs about +25-28% constant currency with the rupee down about 9% YoY, against Q1 FY27's +16.1% cc. The same vendor consensus overshot Q2 FY26 revenue by 13.2% (Zacks, https://finance.yahoo.com/news/makemytrip-mmyt-q2-earnings-revenues-122502393.html), so it looks mis-specified. EPS consensus is $0.03-0.04, which reads as an IFRS-basis figure: Q1 printed $0.53 adjusted against a $0.22 'consensus'. That makes the EPS bar disputed. The stock trades on gross bookings, adjusted margin and adjusted operating profit (Q1: 1.8% of gross bookings, which management guided to stay 'around 1.8%'), and no sourced consensus exists for those. print_vs_bar_pct is measured against the $268M revenue bar and assumes about 16% cc growth less 9 points of FX, roughly $245-250M. Findings that depend on the revenue bar are capped small.
first_hunter_context.positioning_check: Short interest was 8,233,580 shares on the 2026-09-30 record date, 9.76% of float, 8.5 days to cover, up 3.5% from 7.96M (MarketBeat, https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NASDAQ/MMYT/short-interest/). An aggregator snippet gave about 9.0M shares and 12.3 days to cover on 2026-08-14 (https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/mmyt/short-interest/, snippet_only, page 403). Part of this is probably convertible-arbitrage hedging against about $1.6B of convertible notes, so not all of it is a directional short. Even so, it is moderately crowded, which shrinks the negatives. The skew is +6.56 vol points (downside paid) and put/call OI is 9.27, but total OI is only 1,161 and the ATM spread is 60% of mid, so the option lean is indicative only. The stock is down 52% from its 52-week high, -8% over 20 days and -7.7% over 5 days, and trades below its 50-day average of $52.08. Hedge-fund holders fell from 26 to 14 over Q2 (Insider Monkey, 2026-10-08).

evidence.text: Industry domestic air volume weakened through the reported quarter, more than in Q1. DGCA/ICRA put July 2026 at 12.0M passengers (-4.8% YoY, capacity -7.8%) and August at 12.126M (-6.34% YoY), against April's -2.0%. On the Aug 3 call management said the seasonal domestic-air drop 'could be larger than usual' and declined to commit to 20%+ cc growth. BofA expects 'a soft 2Q'. Air ticketing was 32% of Q1 adjusted margin and grew only +10.8% cc there.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q4 FY26 (2026-05-19): an air/international deceleration and a cautious outlook sold off about -7.7% to -12%. Q1 FY27 (2026-08-03): air was the weak segment but total bookings beat a low bar, and the stock rose about +8.5%.
evidence.why_not_priced: This is mostly priced. The data is public, management telegraphed it and BofA previewed a soft Q2. What is not visible is the size of the hit to MMYT's air segment: no air-segment consensus is published. If the market had fully priced a worse-than-Q1 air quarter, the revenue consensus would not sit at an implied +17% reported. The rest of the company (hotels and packages 43%, bus 17%, others 8% of adjusted margin) grew 21-32% cc in Q1 and has positive peer reads (see the IHCL and ixigo bus findings), so this is sized net of that.
evidence.independence: Management call summary, Aug 2026: https://www.webull.com/news/15378440584635392. BofA preview quoted by Investing.com, 2026-10-23: https://uk.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/makemytrip-earnings-on-deck-as-india-travel-faces-fuel-headwinds-93CH-4928927

evidence.text: Indian Hotels (IHCL) reported Q2 FY27 on 2026-10-21, after MMYT's last print. Consolidated revenue rose 21% YoY and standalone revenue 26%. Search-snippet summaries put domestic same-store RevPAR at about +25%. IHCL raised its FY27 revenue-growth guide from 12-14% to 15-17%. That points to strong domestic hotel demand in Jul-Sep for MMYT's hotels and packages segment, its largest at 43% of Q1 adjusted margin and +21.3% cc in Q1.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 FY27: hotels and packages +21.3% cc carried a bookings beat, and the stock rose about +8.5%.
evidence.why_not_priced: MMYT fell about 7.7% in the five sessions that include this release, so the ADR has not traded on the read-through. If it had, the stock would not be making new lows into the print with downside skew bid. This is a proxy: IHCL is luxury and upper-upscale, and MMYT's hotels line includes weak outbound packages, so it is sized small.
evidence.independence: ixigo Q2 FY27 (2026-10-17) hotel GTV +159% and room nights +295%, a different document (https://inc42.com/buzz/ixigo-swings-to-₹63-cr-profit-in-q2-revenue-rises-13-yoy/), though from a tiny base.

evidence.text: ixigo (Le Travenues) reported Q2 FY27 on 2026-10-17: bus GTV rose 31.6% YoY to ₹752.7 Cr, passengers +28% and bus revenue +23.8%. ixigo attributed part of that to high airfares pushing intercity travellers to buses. That is a direct counterparty read for MMYT's redBus segment, 17% of Q1 adjusted margin and +32.4% cc in Q1.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Bus has been MMYT's fastest-growing segment (Q1 FY27 +32.4% cc). No resolved print where bus alone drove the reaction.
evidence.why_not_priced: ixigo is an NSE-listed peer that few US ADR holders follow. The read-through is substitution: high airfares push travellers to buses, which offsets part of the air weakness inside MMYT. The ADR fell on the week rather than rising on it. The segment is small, so it is sized small.
evidence.independence: Same document as the ixigo flights finding below. Upstox, 2026-10-19, confirms bus GTV +32%: https://upstox.com/news/market-news/stocks/ixigo-shares-rally-15-as-revenue-soars-13-yo-y-to-321-crore-hotel-gtv-grows-2-6x-check-q2-results/article-202068/

evidence.text: ixigo's Q2 FY27 flights business grew GTV +37.2% and passengers +8%, against an industry domestic market down about 5-6%. Its flight take rate fell from 9.38% to 7% and flight revenue fell 7.5%. Fare inflation is lifting GTV while monetisation compresses, and a smaller rival is buying air share. Both are negative reads for MMYT's air adjusted margin per booking and its air share.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 FY26 (2026-01-21) revenue missed and the stock fell about -8% intraday to -12% close-to-close. Q4 FY26 sold off on air/international deceleration.
evidence.why_not_priced: ixigo's segment take rate is buried in an Indian peer's release. The ADR consensus has no air take-rate line, and BofA's preview frames the problem as supply and volume, not monetisation. ixigo's take-rate fall may be ixigo-specific discounting rather than an airline commission change, so it is sized small.
evidence.independence: Same ixigo document as the bus finding (two readings of one release, opposite segments, so no double count). Industry volume: https://www.angelone.in/news/economy/india-s-domestic-air-traffic-drops-6-34-to-12-126-million-passengers-in-august-2026

evidence.text: Oil re-escalated late in the reported quarter and is still high going into the print. Brent passed $100 on 2026-09-09 for the first time since July (HSBC raised its 2026 forecast to $90, Hormuz flows about 6-10M bpd against 19-20M pre-war) and stood about $107-110 in mid-October. Management's Aug 3 optimism rested on oil having fallen after an MOU, so the Q3 (festive season) commentary on airfares, airline capacity and outbound will probably stay cautious.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q4 FY26 (2026-05-19): a cautious West Asia outlook drove about -7.7% to -12%. MMYT gives no formal guidance, so the outlook commentary is the guide.
evidence.why_not_priced: This is largely priced. The stock fell from about $52 to $43 as oil rose, and the Artisan letter blames the Middle East. What is unpriced is only whether management quantifies a festive-quarter slowdown. This is macro-to-company transmission the company has not confirmed since August, so it is sized small.
evidence.independence: Mid-October Brent about $107-110 (Economie Matin citing Reuters, 2026-10-19): https://www.economiematin.fr/?p=234386. Management's Aug 3 framing that demand recovered after oil fell: https://www.webull.com/news/15378440584635392
